messages.subject: Re: [seewave] spec() amplitude units
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

could you please explain a bit more what happens if you set norm= FALSE.
I have problems grasping the output of the spec () function when setting norm =false

I want to apllie it to a .wav file to get "absolute" amplitude values at a specific time point. The description says: "Results can be obtained either as absolute or dB data". But I am do not understand what "absolute" amplitude means in the context of this function.

I just started working with seewave and analysis of soundfiles so please forgive if I am asking something that should be obviouse to anybody else.

Kind regards
Sandra

On Tuesday, 4 March 2014 13:30:14 UTC+1, Jérôme SUEUR wrote:
> Hi,
>
> By default, the spectrum amplitude is scaled by its maximum but you
> can turn the argument norm to FALSE to get not scaled amplitude values.
>
> Jerome
>
>
> Quoting rob <robhi...@gmail.com>:
>
> >
> > Hi,
> >
> > I am using spec() on acceleration data (unit: m/s2).
> >
> > code:
> >
> > spec(wave=data, wn ="hanning", f=sampfreq, norm=F, wl=windowlen, plot=F)
> >
> > My question is, given the output of this function call, are the units of
> > "amplitude" (y-axis) the same as in the original data passed to the "wave"
> > parameter (i.e m/s2)?
> >
> > Thanks
